newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude market seen well supplied.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude market seen well supplied.

text.p: The U.S. West Coast crude market was seen well supplied on Monday amid ample supply, with Friday's Alaska North Slope cargo sale by Chevron to Shell setting a weaker tone for the market.

That October-delivery deal for the regional benchmark was done at a $2.15 a barrel discount to the West Texas Intermediate marker, which brings the decline in the differential to 30 cents over the past month.
"It's still a crude buyers' market. I expect we'll continue to trade at between 65 pct and 67 pct of WTI into next spring," said a major oil company trader.
Among the crude sourced abroad and due into the region soon are Kuwaiti barrels which may push out more ANS onto the local market, traders said.
"I think the next deal you'll see (for ANS) will be around $2.30/$2.40" below WTI, said a West Coast trader.

Meanwhile, local traders said last Friday's fire at a 35,000 barrels-a-day gasoline upgrading unit at Mobil Corp's Torrance, Ca. plant, while helping the products side, was showing no sign of having any effect on the crude market.
A high number of West Coast refinery disruptions in recent months has been a key factor in keeping the regional price differentials under pressure, market players said.
Heavy crude oil prices "are about where they should be," said one trader, noting that Kern River was quoted at discounts of around 35/25 cents to posted pricings at $15.75 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington stood at $17.00/17.20 a barrel, while Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel.
